signals.thesis: Following earlier guidance that it would price at or above its $70 to $78 range, Anthropic priced its upsized IPO at $83 a share, raising over $81 billion in the base offering and $107.3 billion alongside co-founder share sales and a private placement. The deal tops SpaceX's $75 billion base offering as the largest IPO on record, with shares set to begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT and delivering a $3 billion windfall for early investor SK Telecom.
signals.title: Anthropic prices upsized IPO at $83 a share to raise record $81B+

signals.thesis: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, where policymakers held the benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4%, showed officials expect further rate hikes and are concerned about the inflationary impact of AI. Reinforcing the hawkish shift after recent hot inflation data, Fed Governor Christopher Waller urged the central bank to consider a half-percentage-point rate hike at its December meeting to combat inflation remaining above its 2% target.
signals.title: Fed Governor Waller floats 50-bps December hike as FOMC minutes flag AI inflation risks

signals.thesis: Although Nvidia's raised sales forecast under interim CEO Colette Kress initially lifted global tech and U.S. equity futures, the chipmaker's shares ultimately fell 2.9% on Wednesday for a fifth consecutive session of losses. Investors remained unconvinced by the earnings call as the board maintained that ousted CEO Jensen Huang will not be reinstated.
signals.title: Nvidia shares fall 2.9% for fifth straight loss as earnings call fails to calm post-Huang nerves

signals.thesis: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion as it expands its portfolio of cybersecurity tools to counter AI threats. The company's shares rose 7% following its earnings report, helping drive a broader cybersecurity rally that supported technology stocks.
signals.title: Palo Alto Networks acquires AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5B as shares jump 7%

signals.thesis: Satellite and ship-tracking data indicate that outbound liquefied natural gas tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz declined over the past week. The slowdown suggests shipowners are exercising greater caution following a recent flurry of attacks in the Middle East.
signals.title: Outbound LNG tanker traffic through Strait of Hormuz slows after Middle East attacks
